source.rationale: The whole point of the node: say which of the offered companies actually has a matching delivery, under the same product/date filters the customer asked with. Two of three candidates come back with rows (one of them on an ACCOUNT of the company, '... [A/C I]', which must still credit the base name the line was rendered from); the third gets '- no delivery'. THE SEPARATOR IS A PLAIN HYPHEN. The clone body used ' \u2014 has delivery'; U+2014 is banned in customer copy (captain hard rule 2026-08-22) and the sibling annotate-incoming-picker already renders '- has incoming'. A hardcoded literal must not lean on the downstream compose-time sanitizer to fix it. The no-em-dash assertion is in tests/flow/customer-picker.test.js, on the rendered reply, not only here. RETUNED 2026-08-25 (90-day probe window): the probe now always sends a delivery-date window - the parser's own bounds, else an injected last-90-days default - so the miss suffix and the zero-hit close are scoped to that window ('- no delivery in the last 90 days'); a bare '- no delivery' would be a false universal, the probe never looked further back. The parser ctx entry here carries NEITHER date bound, which is exactly the defaulted-window case; hand-annotate-customer-dated-window.json pins the other arm. customer_probe_window_days is the diagnostic mirror of that rule (90 = defaulted window, null = the customer's own dates).
